No question opener, no statistic first, no hypothetical company, no blockquote, no definition sentence.

A horizontal bar from 'which problem' to 'measured after release'; UI design covers the screen segment, UX design the flow segment, digital product design the full span; physical product design and 'digital products to sell' sit off the bar. outline.h2: What does digital product design actually deliver?
outline.answerHint: **Digital product design is the work of deciding what a software product should do, how it should work and how it should look, and it delivers 8 tested artifacts, from a problem brief to developer-ready specs.** (The definition sits inside the deliverables answer; the section is about the hand-over, not the term.)
points: Artifact ledger (visual 1 + astext table): problem brief, research synthesis, user flows and information architecture, wireframes, tested clickable prototype with findings, final UI with all screen states, design system (components + tokens), developer handoff specs with design QA (eav 'deliverables', 'artifact ledger').
One sentence each on the two artifacts founders most often do not get: the problem brief with its success metric, and the screen states.
Role note in one sentence: the person who does this work is often titled 'product designer' in job posts; the title matters less than the artifacts.
Bridge: 'Those artifacts are also how you tell digital product design apart from narrower design work.'

outline.h2: How is digital product design different from UX design, UI design and physical product design?
outline.answerHint: **Digital product design covers the whole span from choosing the problem to measuring the release, while UX design shapes the flow and UI design shapes the screen.**
points: Span bar (visual 2 + astext table): discipline | question owned | typical output | measured by (eav 'difference from UX and UI', hire-product-designer FAQ fact, rephrased).
Physical/industrial product design: same methods, different material; one sentence. 'Digital products to sell' (templates, ebooks, courses) is a different meaning of the words; one sentence, no link.
Do NOT rebuild the hub's 'Product design agency vs a UI design studio' table (that compares providers; this compares disciplines).
Bridge: 'The widest part of that span is the part before any screen exists.'

outline.h2: Which decisions come before anyone draws a screen?
outline.answerHint: **Four decisions come first: the problem worth solving, the user who has it, the metric that will prove the fix, and the constraints the product has to live within.**
points: Problem brief contents in prose (no new table): problem, primary user, success metric (activation, retention or a task metric), constraints (platforms, compliance, budget, deadline).

Elia Wellness (DOWN link /case-studies/elia-wellness/): designing for adults over 50 set the constraints early: plain navigation, readable layouts, a tablet questionnaire with big tap areas and simple rating scales. Facts only from the case study.
Research methods named once with what each settles: interviews (why), analytics review (where), survey (how many). Hub services list item 'User research' (do not restate the list).
Bridge: 'Once those four are written down, the process becomes a matter of raising the evidence behind them.'

outline.h2: How does the digital product design process move from idea to release?
outline.answerHint: **The digital product design process moves from idea to release by raising the evidence at each step, from an assumption to interview patterns, a walked-through flow, a prototype tested with 5 to 8 users and, finally, a measured release.**
points: Evidence ladder (visual 3 + astext ol); eav 'process'. Carrier for 'digital product design process' in sentence 1 or 2.
What 'pass' looks like at each rung (method): e.g. at the prototype rung, most testers finish the core task without help; at the release rung, the agreed metric moves.
Our timings: one sentence + deep link to the hub's 4-stage plan (#how-does-our-product-design-agency-plan-the-work). Do NOT list stage names or week ranges.
Tools in one clause: Figma, FigJam, Maze (hub FAQ).
Bridge: 'The last rung is where design meets the people who build it.'

outline.h2: How do digital product design and development fit together?
outline.answerHint: **Digital product design and development meet at the handoff: design delivers specs, every screen state, components and tokens, then stays in the sprints for design QA until the release is live.**
points: Handoff packet anatomy (visual 4 + astext ul).
Tokens match front-end code; Storybook documents the components (hub FAQ tool list; home.ts design-system line 95 paraphrased).
Design QA: designers review built screens against specs during sprints (hub 'Build support' + stage 'Delivery'), stated as method.

tkxel fact: design and development can run in one contract; teams that already have engineers get annotated Figma files and sprint reviews (home.ts FAQ lines 240, 243). No claim that the designers write code.
Mass Media Co. in one sentence as text only (no link): one partner rethought the workflow and the software, with user interviews, IA, web and mobile app design; +30% order processing efficiency.
Bridge: 'What goes into that packet changes when the product runs on a model or a subscription.'

outline.h2: What changes when the product runs on AI or a subscription?
outline.answerHint: **AI and SaaS products add states that a brochure-style app never has: generated answers that can be wrong, sources to show, corrections to capture, and roles, plans and limits that change what each user sees.**
points: AI: prompt inputs, generated answers, source previews, correction flows, tested with real model output (eav 'AI product states'); add loading and failure states for model calls (method).
SaaS: trials, seats, roles, plan limits, invoices as product surfaces (method; no link to the SaaS silo's posts).

Accessibility and platforms: WCAG 2.2 AA as the US working target (ADA, Section 508), W3C Recommendation October 5, 2023 with 9 new criteria; iOS follows Apple HIG, Android/Flutter follows Material Design 3 (eav rows). Link W3C, Apple, Material once each.
Hub card 'Built for SaaS and AI' paraphrased in one clause (no new link).
Bridge: 'Here is how those pieces looked in products we shipped.'

outline.h2: What does digital product design look like in shipped products?
outline.answerHint: **In shipped products, digital product design shows up as a narrower first version, clearer paths for each audience and a measured change after launch, as our Elia Wellness, Parents Connect, Anyday and Mass Media Co. work shows.**
points: Carrier for 'digital product design examples' in the body (keywordCarrier.secondary).

Case table (text): client | starting point | what design delivered | result as stated. Elia Wellness (idea to product; website, web app, mobile app; +40% registrations), Parents Connect (research-first revamp; web and mobile; +45% forum participation), Anyday (confusing first release, two audiences; employee satisfaction +40%, which the case study ties to immediate wage access), Mass Media Co. (separate tools merged into one platform; +30% order processing efficiency).
One 'we' sentence on the common thread: each started from a written problem and ended with a number the client tracks. Do not attribute any result to design alone.
DOWN link 2: Parents Connect (/case-studies/parents-connect/). Elia was linked in H2 3; Anyday and Mass Media Co. stay plain text (case-study link bucket).
Bridge: 'Portfolios like these are also where you start judging a design team.'

outline.h2: How do you judge design work before you pay for it?
outline.answerHint: **Judge design work by the evidence behind it: a written problem and metric, research the team actually ran, a prototype that real users tested, every screen state designed, and a handoff your engineers can build from.**
points: 7 pass/fail checks (text list): problem + metric stated; research artifacts shown; prototype test findings with participant count; states (empty, loading, error, no permission) in the files; design system with tokens; accessibility target named (WCAG 2.2 AA); design QA during the build.

McKinsey data point (eav 'business value of design'): 32 and 56 percentage points over 5 years for top-quartile design practice, 300 listed companies, correlational, global sample. One sentence on why: the top quartile treats design as measured work, which is what the checks test.
LEAD ANGLE 1 at the end of this section (see leadAngle).
Bridge: 'If the checks show gaps in your own product, the next question is what to buy first.'

outline.h2: Which digital product design work should you buy first?
outline.answerHint: **Buy the step that matches your evidence: discovery if the problem is untested, MVP design if the problem is tested but there is no product, and an ongoing product design engagement if a live product is turning into a patchwork.**
points: Three-door routing map (visual 5 + astext table); eav 'buy-first routing'.

Door 2 links the MVP package (/services/startups/mvp-design-agency/, anchor 'MVP design', the post's ONE cross-hub link). Hub facts allowed in one sentence each: projects start within 1 to 2 weeks of a signed proposal; we often lead research and the design system while in-house designers own feature work.

faqs.q: What is digital product design, in one sentence?
faqs.a: Digital product design decides what a software product does, how it works and how it looks, and tests those decisions with users before and during the build. 2 sentences max; the second names the 8 artifacts as a payoff.

faqs.q: Is a digital product designer the same as a product designer?
faqs.a: Yes, in most US job posts the two titles mean the same software role. Add the difference from a UI UX designer (hire-product-designer FAQ fact, rephrased): a product designer also decides which problem to solve and how to measure it. No salary or career advice.

faqs.q: Does digital product design include development?
faqs.a: No. Design ends with specs, states, components and design QA during the build; engineers write the code. Our team is part of tkxel, so design and development can run in one contract when you need both (hub FAQ).

faqs.q: How long does digital product design take?
faqs.a: It depends on the evidence you already have: discovery for one product area is weeks, a full product with a design system is months. Point to the hub's stage plan for our timings (link only if the link builder allows a 3rd hub link; otherwise plain text 'our stage plan'). Most projects start within 1 to 2 weeks of a signed proposal.

faqs.q: Can one designer handle digital product design for a startup?
faqs.a: Yes, for a narrow scope such as one flow or a first prototype; research, a design system, web and mobile together usually need more than one person. If the BLS figure is verified, add the median pay for web and digital interface designers as an input for in-house cost. No link to /services/hire-product-designer/ (cross-hub cap).

CASE STUDIES (exact facts only): Elia Wellness: LMS for adults over 50; scope 'strategy and the path from idea to product, plus the website, the web app and the mobile app'; five core experiences; seven wellness dimensions in one score; lessons built from text, image, video and challenge blocks; tablet pre-questionnaire with big tap areas and simple rating scales; +40% user registrations; 30+ boost in wellness scores among active users. Do NOT use its quote as a testimonial about design (it thanks the team for 'building'; lesson 2026-10-11). Parents Connect: discovery and stakeholder interviews, product revamp, UX design, brand and visual design; began with research on what parents want; web and mobile; +45% forum participation, +10% average time on the platform. Anyday: product revamp, strategy, web app, mobile app and website; first version hard to navigate; real-time transfers and simplified navigation; two audiences (employees, employers); employee satisfaction +40% 'thanks to immediate access to wages'. Do NOT use the $51,000, 14 hours or the Boston Pizza quote (customer of the client). Mass Media Co.: separate order tools → one platform; discovery workshop with stakeholders and end users defined product, strategy, IA and user flows; +30% order processing efficiency. Never attribute a result to design alone. Do NOT use Nitro ($5M raise), Digno or Vocable figures.

DO NOT USE (unsourced or misquoted figures): 'design-led companies grow 32% faster' (McKinsey says percentage points, over 5 years, top quartile, correlation); any 'every $1 in UX returns $100'; any '88% of users won't return'; Dribbble or marketplace prices; BLS pay unless the fact-checker verifies it on the live page; any '% of startups fail because of design' claim.

DO NOT MIRROR: Wikipedia's 'iterative design process used to solve a functional problem with a formal solution'; Boldare's prototype/MVP/product-market-fit/scaling stages; 'blend of art and science' (SoluteLabs); 'usability and desirability' pairing seen in SERP snippets.

ENTITY SALIENCE: 'digital product design' exact 10–13 uses; H2s 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 and 9 carry it (6 of 9 = 67%, above 40%). Rival entities capped at about 6 uses each: 'UX', 'UI', 'prototype', 'design system', 'handoff', 'MVP'. Use 'digital product design' as the subject of the first sentence in at least 5 of 9 sections. Do not let 'product design agency' compete (anchor only, at most twice).

VOICE: first person by Talha Saleem for method and judgment ('When I hand over a prototype, I attach…'). 'We' only for hub, home.ts, about and case-study facts. No invented anecdotes, clients, timings or rates. Examples beyond the 4 case studies are hypothetical and labeled ('Say you run a scheduling app…'). American spelling.

POST-PUBLISH MONITOR: (a) if Google ranks the hub for 'digital product design' or 'what is digital product design', check that backlink #1 is live and the hubPhrasePlan holds; (b) if the post starts ranking for 'digital product design agency' or 'product design agency', remove any hub-anchor phrase outside links; (c) sister site: see sisterSiteCheck.qaStep (publish blocker).
